- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.3) or shows strong bearish signals, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion or volatility.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day horizon; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for early periods.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0–0.5), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-period SMA or adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% if recent price is above 30-day average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish signals (e.g., 3+ negative entries), model tends to lag; apply 1–2% lag correction to forecast for next period.
